item.title: US Corporate Insiders Are Selling Stocks at a Near Record Pace
item.description: US executives are selling shares at the second-fastest pace in more than 20 years, a classic red flag to some investors because it suggests people with the most corporate knowledge are wary about markets.

item.title: BOJ Is Said Likely to Raise Growth Forecast, Stand Pat on Rates
item.description: The Bank of Japan is likely to consider raising its economic growth forecast at a policy meeting this month while leaving the policy rate unchanged after hiking it to the highest level since 1995, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Amundi Wants Oil, Gas in EU’s New Energy-Transition Fund Class
item.description: Amundi SA wants the European Union to free asset managers to add oil and gas exposures to a new fund category intended to support the transition to a lower-carbon economy.

item.title: Zepto Is Said to Face Sharply Lower Valuation for India IPO
item.description: Indian fast-delivery company Zepto Ltd. is seeking a valuation in an initial public offering sharply below its $7 billion peak as concerns over cash burn temper optimism around the industry and raise questions about the firm’s path to profitability.

item.title: UBS AM’s Zhao Sours on Treasuries as US Growth Outpaces Europe
item.description: UBS Asset Management’s Kevin Zhao is planning to short Treasuries in a bet that the robust US economy will erode the haven appeal of owning government debt.

item.title: US Equity Futures Slide as Chip Selloff Prompts Sector Rotation
item.description: US equity futures fell as a selloff in semiconductor stocks gathered steam, pushing investors to look for alternatives in other corners of the market.

item.title: Why Fed Independence Is Hanging by a Thread
item.description: Last August, President Trump made the unprecedented choice of moving to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook. The administration claimed she was being terminated with cause, citing an ongoing investigation in alleged mortgage fraud committed by Cook. The legal battle between Cook and the administration has been tangled in the courts for the last year, eventually reaching the Supreme Court. item.title: Takaichi Flags Importance of GPIF Investing in Japan Assets
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi flagged the importance of encouraging households and the Government Pension Investment Fund to increase their investment in Japanese financial assets, further fueling expectations of possible allocation changes at the fund.

item.title: China’s Powerful New AI Surprises Investors, Fueling Tech Rout
item.description: A surprise breakthrough from Chinese AI startup Moonshot rippled through global markets Friday, sending AI and semiconductor stocks sharply lower as investors drew parallels with last year’s “DeepSeek moment” and questioned whether the industry’s enormous spending spree is becoming harder to justify.

item.title: Amundi to Book €300 Million Gain From IPO of Indian Venture
item.description: Amundi SA says it expects to book net capital gain of around €300 million ($343 million) from the initial public offering of its asset management joint venture in India.

item.title: UBS, Deutsche Bank Raise Stoxx 600 Targets as European Stocks Rally
item.description: Accelerating earnings growth and confidence the rally can withstand the latest geopolitical jitters means strategists are increasingly optimistic about European stocks, a Bloomberg survey shows.

item.title: Philippine Bourse Seeks to Boost Retail Trading With New Reforms
item.description: The sole stock exchange in the Philippines is preparing a slew of measures including new exchange-traded funds to attract retail investors away from online gambling and cryptocurrency trading.

item.title: Manipal Hospitals Said to Cut Valuation to $8.3 Billion in IPO
item.description: India’s Manipal Health Enterprises Ltd., operator of the Manipal Hospitals chain, is seeking a lower valuation of about 800 billion rupees ($8.3 billion) in its planned initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: SoftBank Plans New ¥60 Billion Bond After Retail, Overseas Deals
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. plans to sell about ¥60 billion ($369 million) of notes to institutional investors in Japan this month after domestic retail and foreign-currency bond offerings earlier this year.

item.title: Abu Dhabi’s ADIC Hires BlackRock Veteran to Lead Real Assets
item.description: The Abu Dhabi Investment Council has hired a former BlackRock Inc. and Macquarie Group executive to lead its real assets business, underscoring the emirate’s ability to attract senior global investment talent despite regional geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Z.AI Set to Be First China AI Firm With $1 Billion Annual Sales
item.description: Z.AI is on track for annual recurring revenue of $1 billion, a significant ramp-up for an enterprise-focused AI startup trying to fend off a host of rivals in an intensely competitive Chinese field.

item.title: Michael Burry Says ‘Good Time’ to Chase Hong Kong Stock Bargains
item.description: Michael Burry, the investor made famous in The Big Short, recommends bargain hunting in Hong Kong’s stock market after it lagged peers during the global AI rally this year.

item.title: Palm Oil Heads for Weekly Gain on India Demand, Biofuel Outlook
item.description: Palm oil headed for a second weekly advance on expectations for stronger demand from India, and a lift from higher crude prices.

item.title: FSTE 100 Live: European Stocks Set to Drop as AI Anxiety Spoils Sentiment
item.description: FSTE 100 Live: European Stocks Set to Drop as AI Anxiety Spoils Sentiment【原文：FSTE 100 Live: European Stocks Set to Drop as AI Anxiety Spoils Sentiment】

item.title: Coronation Trims TSMC, SK Hynix on AI Hype, Boosts India Stocks
item.description: Coronation Asset Management Ltd., which oversees $47 billion, has trimmed its exposure to chipmakers and increased its allocation to India, as expectations for artificial intelligence stocks have risen to levels that are nearly impossible to beat.

item.title: NSE Stock Draws Rare ‘Sell’ Call Ahead of Long-Awaited IPO Debut
item.description: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., the operator of the world’s largest derivatives exchange by trading volume, has received a ‘sell’ recommendation just as it gears up to launch the country’s biggest initial public offering.

item.title: Wheat Eases as Traders Lock In Gains, Assess Black Sea Threats
item.description: Wheat extended a decline as traders took profits, against a backdrop of Black Sea supply risks and weak US export demand.

item.title: RBI Governor Flags Elevated Inflation, Monsoon as Key Risks
item.description: India’s inflation remains elevated, with ongoing tensions in the Middle East and prospects of a weak monsoon season seen as key risks for the economy, according to Reserve Bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra.

item.title: Howden Plots Giant Capital Raise on Path to Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Howden Group, the London-based insurance broker that’s chasing an initial public offering by 2030, is in talks to raise several billion pounds in new private capital as it seeks to maintain its break-neck expansion.

item.title: Japan LDP Seeks to Rein in ‘Excessive’ Activist Proposals
item.description: A Japanese ruling party panel is calling for stricter limits on shareholder rights, arguing that existing regulations encourage what it sees as “excessive” activist proposals and the pursuit of short-term profits.

item.title: Eoptolink Is Said to File for Up to $5 Billion Hong Kong Listing
item.description: Eoptolink Technology Inc., a Chinese maker of optical transceivers, has filed confidentially for a multibillion-dollar listing in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: ECB Set to Wait for September to Hike One Last Time, Poll Shows
item.description: The European Central Bank will probably pause to assess inflation next week before delivering a final interest-rate hike in September, economists say.

item.title: Malaysian Growth Surges to 5.8% as Services, Tech Sales Counter Impact of War
item.description: Malaysia reported a surprise surge in economic growth in the second quarter as robust services and electronics exports countered the impact of the war in the Middle East.

item.title: EU’s Answer to Trump’s Bank Deregulation Agenda: Explainer
item.description: Bank bosses in the European Union will turn their attention to Brussels this afternoon when the bloc’s executive arm lays out its long-awaited answer to the deregulatory agenda championed by US President Donald Trump.

item.title: EM Stocks Headed For Weekly Loss on Tech Selloff, Rising Crude
item.description: Emerging-market equities fell for a second day and are headed for a weekly decline as concerns over stretched AI valuations dragged technology shares lower, triggering a selloff across Asia.
